title: Vision Navigation
description: Per-drone configuration for the ADOS Vision Navigation plugin.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Operating mode. Optical flow uses a downward camera + rangefinder. VIO modes accept a forward or downward camera (orientation chosen per the camera block). Hybrid runs both estimators in parallel from two cameras.

secondary_camera.title: Secondary camera
secondary_camera.description: Only used by hybrid_of_plus_vio. The primary camera carries the downward optical-flow stream; the secondary carries the forward VIO stream. Both orientations must be set explicitly.

rangefinder.title: Rangefinder
rangefinder.description: Distance source used to scale optical flow into metric velocity.

topology.title: Topology
topology.description: Where the rangefinder is wired. companion = plugin reads it; fc = flight controller already publishes DISTANCE_SENSOR; none = no rangefinder.

device.title: Device node
device.description: Serial device path (for example /dev/ttyUSB0) for UART drivers, or an I2C bus identifier (digit such as "1" or path such as /dev/i2c-1) for I2C drivers. Optional when topology is fc or none.

type.title: Firmware
type.description: Flight controller firmware. Optical flow is supported on ArduPilot, PX4, and iNav (7.0+). VIO is supported on ArduPilot and PX4; on iNav it is experimental and disabled by the plugin at install time. Betaflight is not supported because the firmware has no position estimator.

ekf_source_set_index.title: EKF source set index
ekf_source_set_index.description: ArduPilot EK3_SRCn set (1-3) that selects the vision-flow source group.

pre_arm.title: Pre-arm origin
pre_arm.description: Optional pre-arm helper that pushes a synthetic origin when the firmware refuses to arm without one.

device_path.title: Device path
device_path.description: V4L2 or CSI device node (for example /dev/video0).

orientation.title: Mount orientation
orientation.description: Direction the lens points. Downward suits over-ground flight (agriculture, survey, SAR, pipeline patrol) where ground texture is dense. Forward suits indoor or corridor flight. Side is reserved for future SLAM use cases. Auto infers from the bound HAL camera role; only safe when the board profile declares orientation unambiguously.
